headlines: round-56's '-25.2 ms, 12/12 faster' tokenize prefetch is RETRACTED: it was a measurement-path artefact (experiment-only synchronize in compute). On the exact entry loop the faithful prefetch is SLOWER: 12/12, median +27.7 ms.

the round-56 / run-1 prefetch implementation was NOT numerically equivalent to the entry (loss re-implemented outside autocast): micro-0 loss 0.927814 vs 0.917383, 386/386 dense grads differ (max_abs 0.008789).

forward gaps are now attributed with explicit markers: of the 28 forward gaps >= 2 ms in the profiled entry-loop trace (3 steps) 25 are tokenizer-dominated (94-98% of the gap); forward UNKNOWN is 0.76 ms in total (0.8%). What is left stays UNKNOWN.

NEW SCOPE LIMIT: bitwise reproducibility on this device was observed only for runs that repeat an identical run pattern - with another run pattern 4/4 native fresh processes differ (hit-step grad norm 10.6875-11.9375). All 'bitwise identical' results are same-state, same-pattern comparisons; multi-step trajectories of native itself vary at the ulp level.

in the unprofiled entry the forward phase is device-bound: the pageable H2D copy is a full stream sync (host blocked 245 ms/step inside move_features) but removing it (pinned + non_blocking, bitwise-identical state) does not change the step time (-1.8 ms median, CI [-10.1, +8.1]).

dW Python route: training state bitwise identical (386/386 dense grads, 391/391 params, optimizer state); on the entry loop diff-in-diff -9.0 ms, 95% CI [-17.5, -0.6], 13/14 processes negative; ~0.4% of a step, candidate only.

item1_training_state_consistency.command: for c in dw_route prefetch_faithful prefetch_loss_reimpl prefetch_loss_reimpl_run1 h2d_nonblocking; do python3 examples/retrieval/train_state_consistency.py --conf examples/retrieval/conf/run/bge_m3_ppu.yaml --candidate $c --out results/train_state_r57.json; done; python3 examples/retrieval/train_state_consistency.py --merge --out results/train_state_r57.json
item1_training_state_consistency.design: ONE process per candidate: after 2 warmup optimizer steps one snapshot (model, optimizer state, CPU+CUDA RNG, the 4 micro-batches) is taken; native x3 from the snapshot, then the candidate is installed and run x2 from the same snapshot. Each run = one optimizer step of the ORIGINAL entry loop (loss under autocast via the untouched loss_for_batch, isfinite(loss) host sync, backward, clip_grad_norm_, optimizer.step).
item1_training_state_consistency.rng_dropout_data_order: CPU and CUDA RNG states are restored from the snapshot before every run (dropout masks identical); the 4 micro-batches are deep-copied in the snapshot (data order fixed); tokenization has no randomness; the prefetch worker thread consumes no torch RNG.

thresholds.basis: 2% relative error floored at 1% of the tensor's max |value| (bf16 mantissa); params by absolute error; the verdict distinguishes bitwise identity from within-threshold

item1_training_state_consistency.embedding_tables: word / position / token_type embedding gradients come from an index-accumulating backward whose summation order is not reproducible on this device: native-vs-native differs on exactly these tensors in every native pair. Reported separately, excluded from the candidate verdict.

Only the 3 embedding tables differ, and native-vs-native differs on the same tables (device accumulation-order non-determinism).

item1_training_state_consistency.cross_process_warning: SCOPE (round-57): the bitwise comparisons of this file are between runs that repeat an identical run pattern inside one process (same ops, same synchronization points, same restored snapshot). With THIS script five fresh processes reproduced the native state exactly (post-hit-step dense-parameter sha256 b133cb9f..., loss 0.917383, grad norm 9.5). With a different run pattern the native warmup was NOT reproducible, not even across fresh processes (route_from_step0_r57.*.native_from_start_*.json: 4 processes, 4 different states) - see summary_r57.json reproducibility_scope; the cause is not determined. The first r57 attempt ran the candidate in another process with the route registered before the warmup (loss0 0.95186 vs 0.94985); it was discarded as a comparison and is NOT evidence of cross-process non-determinism.
item1_training_state_consistency.invalid_first_version: commit fc2a466e carried a prefetch_loss_reimpl_run1 comparison whose NATIVE baseline had been run WITHOUT autocast (script bug: the candidate's outer-autocast flag also applied to the native runs; native param sha256 509df944... instead of b133cb9f..., native loss 0.928161 instead of 0.917383). Its numbers (loss 0.928161 vs 0.927814, grad norm 9.9375 vs 9.5, grad max_abs 0.6875, optimizer-state max_abs 7.2e-3) were artefacts of that and are withdrawn. Corrected run: natives use the entry path.
item1_training_state_consistency.verdict: overlap (prefetch_faithful) vs inline, same snapshot: PASS bitwise - every dense gradient / post-update parameter / optimizer-state tensor identical in all 7 candidate pairs, losses and grad norms equal, 0 non-finite; only the 3 index-accumulated embedding tables differ, and native-vs-native differs on the same tables. The round-56 / run-1 implementation (prefetch_loss_reimpl_run1) FAILS: it is a different computation, not a prefetch of the same one.

item3_forward_gap_markers.method: device gaps = union of kernel/gpu_memcpy/gpu_memset intervals per step; per gap every category interval is CLIPPED to the gap, then unioned, then made exclusive in priority order (tokenizer > prepare_embedding_inputs > h2d > next_batch > loss_sync > python_gc > launch_submit > blocking_runtime > other_runtime > cpu_op); UNKNOWN = gap - covered. next_kernel = first device event after the gap, with the host time of its launch call relative to the gap start. No neighbourhood attribution.

categories.loss_sync: MK_loss_sync: the entry's isfinite(loss) host sync (entry loop)
categories.blocking_runtime: *Synchronize / cudaMemcpy / cudaMalloc / cudaFree / cudaStreamQuery ... call duration
categories.cpu_op: aten op dispatch intervals not inside the above

item3_forward_gap_markers.r36_note: the r36 trace itself cannot be marked retro-actively; the capture-loop run repeats its exact loop and window (steps 2-4) with the markers added. r36's largest gap (19.24 ms in s2) did not recur (largest forward gap here: 5.44 ms).

stage_definitions.prepare_embedding_inputs_ms: host time in the tokenizer + tensorization (20 groups per step)
stage_definitions.h2d_ms: host time blocked in move_features (.to(device), pageable, non_blocking=False)
stage_definitions.forward_launch_ms: host time for the model call to return (kernel issue)

smi_utilization.caveat: utilization.gpu semantics are vendor-defined and not documented for this device; raw distribution only, not a busy-time measurement

gc_hypothesis_test.result: REJECTED: Python GC is 5 collections / 0.4 ms per step (max pause 0.18 ms) and gc.disable() leaves the step time unchanged; the ~2-3.4 ms backward gaps of the profiled trace are not GC. They stay UNKNOWN.

reproducibility_scope.design: every arm: same initial snapshot S0, same batches, CPU+CUDA RNG restored; arms A native, B native again, C mm.out fallback only, D dW route (flag_gems.mm on the whitelisted shapes), E route again; then the hit step on batches 8-11

train_state_consistency_script_native.note: train_state_consistency.py has a different host sync pattern (no gradient copies before clip) - with THAT pattern five fresh processes were identical

reproducibility_scope.finding: Bitwise reproducibility on this device was observed only for runs that repeat an identical run pattern; the cause of the dependence is NOT determined. The native warmup is reproducible across fresh processes with the run pattern of train_state_consistency.py (5/5) but NOT with the run pattern of this script (the two scripts compute the same warmup step and differ only in host-side work around it: gradient copies to host before clip, an initial parameter hash, batches fetched before the micro steps): 4 native processes give 4 different states (hit-step micro-0 loss 0.944580-0.951953, grad norm 10.6875-11.9375); in-process replays of the native path from the same initial snapshot differ in 293/386 dense step-0 gradient tensors (max_abs 0.001953). With the dW route registered before the warmup: 3 processes, 3 different states (grad norm 9.125-13.5).

route_vs_native_in_process.reading: same magnitudes as native vs native (A vs B): no route-specific effect is visible at this level, and none can be excluded at the ulp level

consequences: Every 'bitwise identical' statement in this PR (r43 frozen dW operands, r44/r46 hit step, r57 snapshot replay) is a same-state comparison between runs with an identical run pattern. None of them is a statement about whole-trajectory equality.

The r46 'cross-process rebuild 0/72' result is an instance of this (different run conditions), not evidence of a candidate effect. The first r57 attempt's phase A/B discrepancy is likewise NOT attributed to cross-process rebuild; the explanation given in commits fc2a466e / cea8f018 is withdrawn.

Multi-step trajectory differences of ulp origin (native hit-step grad norm 10.6875-11.9375, micro-0 loss 0.944580-0.951953 across 4 processes) cannot be used to compare candidates; same-state single-step replay is the valid instrument.

dW route registered before the warmup: variability across 3 processes (grad norm 9.125-13.5) vs native 10.6875-11.9375; too few runs to say whether the route widens the native band (flag_gems.mm uses triton.autotune and has a Stream-K path). OPEN.

loop_fidelity_disclosure.note: rounds <= 56 timed whole steps on the r36 capture loop (no lookahead, no isfinite(loss) sync). The ORIGINAL entry loop is slower by the amounts below; all r57 timing uses the entry loop.

answers.stable_gain: NONE that is deployable. Prefetch: +27.7 ms (slower). H2D non-blocking: -1.8 ms (no significant difference). dW Python route: -9.0 ms [-17.5, -0.6] on 42+42 paired steps, bitwise-identical training state, candidate only (~0.4%).
answers.time_breakdown: per step (entry loop, median step 2127.11 ms of steps 2-4: 1898.07 / 2127.11 / 2351.47): backward GEMM 772 ms device (38% of kernel time), backward attention 375 ms (18.5%), forward GEMM 330 ms (16.2%), forward attention 205 ms (10.1%) [r36 kernel times]; host over 12 steps: tokenize 65.67 ms (3.03% of step), H2D block 252.44 ms (waiting for the device), loss sync 118.78 ms (waiting for the device), backward launch 1425.68 ms (host held by the launch queue). Forward gaps in the profiled entry-loop trace: ~42.4 ms/step in gaps >= 2 ms, of which tokenizer ~27.9 ms/step; UNKNOWN ~0.3 ms/step (forward) + ~10.7 ms/step (backward, profiled only). Unprofiled device utilization (SMI): median 96%.
answers.counter_backed: none for HBM / matrix units (PCM blocked). The only device-side measurement added in r57 is SMI utilization sampling (vendor-defined semantics, median 96%, raw distribution reported).
